Patch Set 27:

(2 comments)

Tachless fan support in the relationship chain is not required for this code, but basing it on that makes it easy to test this out on HPE hardware.

Currently, I'm thinking I'm going to split the 'tachless fan support' PR into 2 smaller, but logically separated PRs -- one with the HPE-specific changes, and one that only includes code that should make FanSensor more readable for anyone without affecting any underlying logic (beyond expected starting points for string manipulations).

I'm thinking I might promote this PR and that upcoming 'not-HPE specific' one at being FanSensor fixup without in-depth understanding required -- which would also make it easier to get the HPE-specific (specific tachless fan support) included on top of it all later.

Done.

The (non-critical) parent PRs for this gerrit are now split into:

83209: fan path disambiguation+ | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/83209 

82362: tachless fan support | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/82362
I'm probably going to add more comments later around the main sensorTypes loop added in this PR -- but I think this should be a good start to explaining things.

sensorTypes is redefined below as an array populated by FanConfigPair structs -- which store these strings as 'configName' 

References to sensorTypes have all been updated accordingly.
static_assert below is no longer needed because the arrays no longer need to be synced.
Fan logic in the daemon below no longer needs to distinguish between specific non-i2c fan types -- so we've replaced those FanType entries above with FanType::BmcBuiltIt

cfgIntf is now set inside a nested loop that cycles through each fanType.

Reasoning:

As we loop through all the SensorConfiguration objects passed into this callback, we know they're all fan sensor records, but we don't know which type -- AspedFan, NuvotonFan, HPEFan, I2CFan ect.

a vital 'sensorBase' lookup currently works by querying for a specific configuration interface (xyz.openbmc_project.Configuration.Aspeedfan or .HPEFan, ect.) 

Setting cfgIntf inside the new loop ensures we'll keep querying for the sensorBase with each valid fan interface type until we find the handle we want from the SensorConfig object.

-------------

A future improvement might be to try and find sensorBase without doing the lookup via interface type, but I'm not sure it would save that many cycles with the short (and unlikely to grow, after this improvement) list of valid fan type strings to watch for -- but I'm not sure how that would work yet (see the 

>auto sensorBaseFind = cfgData.find(cfgIntf);

call around line 366 for the lookup in question.

The 'red' code (logic) here is virtually unchanged, except it's moved into the SensorsType loop. 

This doesn't change overall behavior because the SensorsTypes loop will only get to this point when we've already found the appropriate interface matches to run through the entire process once per valid record match.
The logic below no longer relies on
Done

GenericFan?

If we wanted, it should be simple to add an entry for string 'GenericFan' and have future EMConfigs use that 'type' to call out fan stanzas. 

Existing Fan Types would continue to work, but could also be seemlessly swapped out in existing EMConfigs.

Could be turned into a new Gerrit PR for further discussion if folks particularly like the sound of that... (comment here to vote on that :)

I agree with the premise, I dislike the name "GenericFan".  It should be something like "BmcConnectedFan" so the name is able to be disambiguated directly without documentation.

"GenericFan" could mean anything.

I like that 'BmcConnectedFan' would tell you exactly what it is. 

It's such a small change to add support, so I went ahead and just added it as an option while alphabetizing the FanTypes::BmcBuiltIn items.

the indexVal check allows us to know if the new sensorTypes loop ended without making an hwmon pwm index -> Entity-Manager fan index match first. 

This mean the fan record (SensorConfiguration object) being scanned didn't have an index # (as called out in the Entity-Manager fan stanza) that matches against the index # of the fanOutputPath (ie ../hwmon0/pwm1'). In that case, move onto the nexst SensorObject and do the same checks.

We need an index match to continue the rest of the process.
Adjusts for the new sensorTypes array contents, but logic is the same as before.
Adjusts for the new sensorTypes array contents, but logic is the same as before.

we loop over a list of possible sensorTypes to discover which one the current sensorConfiguration object contains.

Once a match is found (setting sensorBase and matching the index), this loop will exit, and sensor creation steps will continue like normal.
Note: The logic below this point is more-or-less a straight copy/paste of code from below, moved inside this loop to account for the new method of looping over fanTypes til a match is found.
Would've liked to see this kepth alphabetical, but nbd.
Monkey's paw curls -- the named fans are in alphabetical order now, but there's a new "BmcConnectedFan" item added to top billing
I'm not sure I understand why BmcConnectedFan comes alphabetically before AspeedFan.... but this list wasn't alphabetical before, so I won't hold you to it.
